All mu pointers refer to the first column of\n// the segment; the x neighbours are part of the halo of the mu tile, so no clamping is needed.\nstatic inline void updateRow(const double* __restrict cold, const double* __restrict mc,\n                             const double* __restrict myn, const double* __restrict myp,\n                             const double* __restrict mzn, const double* __restrict mzp,\n                             double* __restrict cnew, const size_t n) noexcept {\n    constexpr double fac = params::dt * params::D;\n\n#pragma omp simd\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        cnew[i] = cold[i] + fac * laplacianCell(mc[i], mc[i - 1], mc[i + 1], myn[i], myp[i],\n                                                mzn[i], mzp[i]);\n    }\n}\n\n// Blocking of the iteration space into tiles that are processed by a single thread each.\n// The chemical potential is never materialized for the whole grid: every tile keeps a rolling\n// window of three mu planes in the private cache, which fuses both sweeps of a time step into a\n// single pass over the grid and cuts the memory traffic roughly in half.\nstruct Tiling {\n    size_t xb = 1, yb = 1, zb = 1;     // tile extents\n    size_t nxb = 1, nyb = 1, nzb = 1;  // number of tiles per dimension\n    size_t rowStride = 1;              // elements per mu row (tile width + halo + padding)\n    size_t planeCap they are fixed, so they are compile time constants\nnamespace params {\nconstexpr double dx = 1.0;\nconstexpr double dy = 1.0;\nconstexpr double dz = 1.0;\nconstexpr double dt = 0.01;\nconstexpr double e_AA = -(2.0 / 9.0);\nconstexpr double e_BB = -(2.0 / 9.0);\nconstexpr double e_AB = (2.0 / 9.0);\nconstexpr double gamma = 0.5;\nconstexpr double D = 1.0;\n}  // namespace params\n\n// Laplacian of a single cell from its (already clamped) neighbour values\nstatic inline double laplacianCell(const double v, const double xn, const double xp,\n                                   const double yn, const double yp,\n                                   const double zn, const double zp) noexcept {\n    constexpr double dx = params::dx;\n    constexpr double dy = params::dy;\n    constexpr double dz = params::dz;\n\n    const double cxx = (xp + xn - 2.0 * v) / (dx * dx);\n    const double cyy = (yp + yn - 2.0 * v) / (dy * dy);\n    const double czz = (zp + zn - 2.0 * v) / (dz * dz);\n\n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// Chemical potential of a single cell\nstatic inline double muCell(const double cv, const double xn, const double xp,\n                            const double yn, const double yp,\n                            const double zn, const double zp) noexcept {\n    constexpr double e_AA = params::e_AA;\n    constexpr double e_BB = params::e_BB;\n    constexpr double e_AB = params::e_AB;\n    constexpr double gamma = params::gamma;\n\n    return 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * e_BB - 2.0 * cv * e_AB)\n           + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n           - gamma * laplacianCell(cv, xn, xp, yn, yp, zn, zp);\n}\n\n// Chemical potential for the x range [xlo, xhi] (inclusive) of one row; ny, const size_t nz, const size_t nthreads) {\n    // Rolling mu window budget; small enough for two SMT siblings to share an L2 cache\n    constexpr size_t bufferBudget = 64 * 1024;\n    constexpr i + 4 <= n; i += 4) {\n        _mm256_stream_pd(dst + i, _mm256_loadu_pd(src + i));\n    }\n#endif\n    for (; i < n; ++i) dst[i] = src[i];\n}\n\n// Blocking of the iteration space into tiles that are processed by a single thread each.\n// The chemical potential is never materialized for the whole grid: every tile keeps a rolling\n// window of three mu planes in the private cache, which fuses both sweeps of a time step into a\n// single pass over the grid and cuts the memory traffic roughly in half.\nstruct Tiling {\n    size_t xb = 1, yb = 1, zb = 1;     // tile extents\n    size_t nxb = 1, nyb = 1, nzb = 1;  // number of tiles per dimension\n    size_t rowStride = 1;              // elements per mu row (tile width + halo + padding)\n    size_t planeCap = 1;               // elements per mu plane\n};\n\nstatic Tiling makeTiling(const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz, const size_t nthreads) {\n    // Rolling mu window budget; small enough for two SMT siblings to share an L2 cache\n    constexpr size_t bufferBudget = 64 * 1024;\n    constexpr size_t maxTileWidth = 256;\n\n    Tiling t;\n    t.nxb = (nx + maxTileWidth - 1) / maxTileWidth;\n    if (t.nxb < 1) t.nxb = 1;\n    t.xb = (nx + t.nxb - 1) / t.nxb;\n    // One halo column on each side, padded so that every mu row starts on a cache line\n    t.rowStride = (t.xb + 2 + 7) / 8 * 8 + 8;\n\n    t.yb = ny;\n    while (t.yb > 1 && 3 * t.rowStride * (t.yb + 2) * sizeof(double) > bufferBudget) {\n        t.yb = (t.yb + 1) / 2;\n    }\n\n    const auto derive = [&]() {\n        t.nyb = (ny + t.yb - 1) / t.yb;\n        const size_t planar = t.nxb * t.nyb;\n        size_t nzb = (nthreads + planar - 1) / planar;\n        if (nzb > nz) nzb = nz;\n        if (nzb < 1) nzb = 1;\n        t.zb = (nz + nzb - 1) / nzb;\n        t.nzb = (nz + t.zb - 1) / t.zb;\n    };\n    derive();\n\n    // Flat tiles recompute a large fraction of the mu planes at their z borders; Once the grid no longer\n// fits into the last level cache, the write allocate traffic of ordinary stores costs more than\n// the extra L1 round trip through the row buffer (the values themselves are untouched, so the\n// result is bit identical to the direct store path).\nstatic inline void streamRow(double* __restrict dst, const double* __restrict src,\n                             const size_t n) noexcept {\n    size_t i = 0;\n#if defined(__AVX__)\n    while (i < n && (reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(dst + i) & 31u) != 0) {\n        dst[i] = src[i];\n        ++i;\n    }\n    for (;     // tile extents\n    size_t nxb = 1, nyb = 1, nzb = 1;  // number of tiles per dimension\n    size_t rowStride = 1;              // elements per mu row (tile width + halo + padding)\n    size_t planeCap = 1;               // elements per mu plane\n};\n\nstatic Tiling makeTiling(const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz, const size_t nthreads) {\n    // Rolling mu window budget; small enough for two SMT siblings to share an L2 cache\n    constexpr size_t bufferBudget = 64 * 1024;\n    constexpr size_t maxTileWidth = 256;\n\n    Tiling t;\n    t.nxb = (nx + maxTileWidth - 1) / maxTileWidth;\n    if (t.nxb < 1) t.nxb = 1;\n    t.xb = (nx + t.nxb - 1) / t.nxb;\n    // One halo column on each side, padded so that every mu row starts on a cache line\n    t.rowStride = (t.xb + 2 + 7) / 8 * 8 + 8;\n\n    t.yb = ny;\n    while (t.yb > 1 && 3 * t.rowStride * (t.yb + 2) * sizeof(double) > bufferBudget) {\n        t.yb = (t.yb + 1) / 2;\n    }\n\n    const auto derive = [&]() {\n        t.nyb = (ny + t.yb - 1) / t.yb;\n        const size_t planar = t.nxb * t.nyb;\n        size_t nzb = (nthreads + planar - 1) / planar;\n        if (nzb > nz) nzb = nz;\n        if (nzb < 1) nzb = 1;\n        t.zb = (nz + nzb - 1) / nzb;\n        t.nzb = (nz + t.zb - 1) / t.zb;\n    };\n    derive();\n\n    // Flat tiles recompute a large fraction of the mu planes at their z borders; z < z1; ++z) {\n        if (z == z0) {\n            const size_t zstart = (z > 0) ? z - 1 : 0;\n            const size_t zend = (z + 1 < nz) ? z + 1 : z;\n            for (size_t zz = zstart; zz <= zend; y < y1; ++y) {\n            const size_t yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n            const size_t yp = (y + 1 < ny) ? y + 1 : y;\n            const size_t base = z * plane + y * nx + x0;\n            if constexpr (Stream) {\n                updateRow(cold + base, muRow(z, y), muRow(z, yn), muRow(z, yp), muRow(zn, y),\n                          muRow(zp, y), rowbuf, width);\n                streamRow(cnew + base, rowbuf, width);\n            } else {\n                updateRow(cold + base, muRow(z, y), muRow(z, yn), muRow(z, yp), muRow(zn, y),\n                          muRow(zp, y), cnew + base, width);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n#if defined(__AVX__)\n    // Make the streaming stores visible before the barrier releases the next time step\n    if constexpr (Stream) _mm_sfence();\n#endif\n}\n\n// The kernel is bandwidth and cache bound, so it depends on stable thread placement and on the\n// first touch NUMA placement staying valid. If the OpenMP runtime does not pin the threads\n// itself (OMP_PROC_BIND unset), pin them here: one thread per physical core, spread over the\n// sockets, only falling back to the SMT siblings once all cores are taken.\n#if defined(__linux__)\n#include <sched.h>\n\nstruct CpuTopology {\n    std::vector<int> order; }\nstatic void bindThreads(int, const CpuTopology&) {}\n#endif\n\n// Initialize concentration field (and first touch both grid buffers with the same tile\n// distribution that the time loop uses)\nvoid initializeConcentration(std::vector<double>& c, std::vector<double>& scratch, const size_t nx,\n                             const size_t ny, const size_t nz, const Tiling& t) {\n    const size_t vol = nx * ny * nz;\n\n#pragma omp parallel for collapse(3) schedule(static) proc_bind(spread)\n    for (size_t zb = 0; The benchmark is parallelized with OpenMP in `cahn-hilliard/cahn_hilliard.cpp` (plus `find_package(OpenMP)` in `CMakeLists.txt`); the executable name is unchanged and no files were added.\n\n**What the parallel version does**\n\n- **Fused sweeps, blocked over the grid.** The two passes (chemical potential, then update) are fused into one pass. `mu` is never materialized for the whole grid; every thread keeps a rolling window of three `mu` planes for its tile in private cache. This roughly halves memory traffic and removes one global barrier per time step.\n- **3D tiling over (x, y, z)**, one tile per thread via `#pragma omp for collapse(3) schedule(static)`, with the `mu` window sized to the L2 budget. The tile shape is derived from the thread count at startup, preferring tall z-slabs (border planes get recomputed, so flat tiles are expensive).\n- **Branch-free vector kernels.** Boundary clamping is hoisted out of the inner loop: y/z clamping into row pointers, x clamping into the tile halo and peeled first/last columns, so the `#pragma omp simd` loops are straight-line.\n- **One persistent parallel region** for the whole time loop; buffers are swapped under `omp single`.\n- **First-touch NUMA init** using the same tile decomposition as the time loop.\n- **Thread placement**: threads are pinned one per physical core (SMT siblings only after all cores are used) when the runtime isn't binding itself; an explicit `OMP_PROC_BIND`/`OMP_PLACES` is respected.\n- **Non-temporal stores** for the result rows, enabled only when the grids exceed the aggregated L3 (detected from sysfs), avoiding write-allocate traffic. Values go through a staging row, so the stored numbers are untouched.\n\n**Correctness:** results are *bit-identical* to the original serial program — verified with `-r`/`-v` (hash, Kahan sum, min/max, samples) over 10 grid shapes (cubic, prime, degenerate `1×7×3`, non-cubic, `600×40×40`) × thread counts 1/3/64/128/255, plus the binding variants. The physical parameters became `constexpr` (they were already fixed constants), which lets the compiler fold the `/(dx*dx)` divisions; this preserves exact FP semantics.\n\n**Measured on the 2×EPYC 7763 host (MCell-updates/s, best of 3):**\n\n| grid | original serial | 1 thread | 64 | 128 (default) | 256 |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 128³ | 165 | 324 | 7232 | 4369 | 2118 |\n| 256³ | 168 | 376 | 13006 | **18137** | 12336 |\n| 384³ | 168 | 227 | 3883 | 4500 | 4560 |\n| 512³ | ~167 | 232 | 5592 | 7158 | 6243 |\n\nThat is ~108x the original at 256³ (48x over the improved single-thread code). Large grids plateau at ~7 GCUPS because they are DRAM-bandwidth-bound — the measured streaming ceiling of this host is ~294 GB/s with NT stores; small grids (≤128³) peak around 64 threads since there is too little work per thread beyond that."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":342,"cache_read_input_tokens":171395,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":342},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5300543a-60c7-40f7-9d11-f0cf722a27c9","uuid":"52f53bd2-6fdc-44e5-b893-bbff9220dc12","timestamp":"2026-09-13T08:43:42.638Z","request_id":"req_011Cf19EhZhRxTJ6FyvSy3L4"}
